question: Should this remain the canonical timeout/fail-open report while a current v0.6.12 or current-main reproduction identifies whether the defect belongs to upstream OpenClaw authentication or the Windows setup integration?
rationale: The report is concrete and was deliberately reopened, but repository inspection cannot safely assign a repo-local repair until the current bundled authentication path is exercised and its credential/polling boundary is observed.

options.title: Retain and reproduce
options.body: Keep this child issue open and capture a current-version device-login transcript plus gateway logs showing completion, expiration, credential state, and restart behavior.

options.title: Route upstream
options.body: If the same failure reproduces in the standalone OpenClaw CLI, preserve this transcript and move implementation ownership to a linked upstream OpenClaw issue.

options.title: Close after verification
options.body: Close only after a current release completes authorization promptly and a source or release change explains why the reported expiration fallthrough can no longer occur.

recommendation.title: Retain and reproduce
recommendation.body: Keep this child issue open and capture a current-version device-login transcript plus gateway logs showing completion, expiration, credential state, and restart behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the linked provider-onboarding tracking issue and most recently made the explicit reopen decision.
